sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: You're sitting in a school bus next to your best friend.
sentences.zh: 你正坐在校车上，旁边是你最好的朋友。

sentences.en: She tells you about the time she stole an eraser from the teacher's desk.
sentences.zh: 她正在向你讲述她当年从老师桌上偷走一块橡皮的故事。

sentences.en: You wonder whether you should tell her about the time you stole a plush toy from a store.
sentences.zh: 你在纠结要不要告诉她，你当年也从商店里偷过一个毛绒玩具。

sentences.en: As the bus rolls along, you go back and forth in your mind and then decide against it.
sentences.zh: 校车在路上颠簸前行，你在心里翻江倒海，最后还是决定不说了。

sentences.en: A few years later, you're at your high school prom.
sentences.zh: 几年后，你参加了高中毕业舞会。

sentences.en: At the end of the evening, you share a kiss with your prom date, who turns out to have bad breath.
sentences.zh: 舞会快结束时，你和舞伴接吻了，结果发现对方有口臭。

sentences.en: This is not someone you are interested in long-term.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个你想长期交往的对象。

sentences.en: Do you share the information or withhold it?
sentences.zh: 你要把这件事说出来，还是咽进肚子里？

sentences.en: Or consider a much more serious situation later in life?
sentences.zh: 或者想想生活中更严肃的情况？

sentences.en: You're in a long-term relationship and you realize that for some years now,
sentences.zh: 你正处于一段长期恋爱中，突然意识到在过去的几年里，

sentences.en: you have been questioning your own sexual orientation.
sentences.zh: 你一直在质疑自己的性取向。

sentences.en: Your partner would be crushed to hear about it.
sentences.zh: 如果你的伴侣听到这个消息，一定会崩溃的。

sentences.en: Things are generally going well in your relationship and you don't have immediate plans to act on your secret feelings.
sentences.zh: 你们的关系目前总体进展顺利，你也没有马上根据这个秘密采取行动的打算。

sentences.en: Is it best to keep them to yourself?
sentences.zh: 最好把这些藏在心里吗？

sentences.en: At every stage of life, we find ourselves confronted with dilemmas like this.
sentences.zh: 在人生的每一个阶段，我们都会面临这样的两难选择。

sentences.en: There is a part of us that wants to share, to have the world see us as we truly are.
sentences.zh: 我们内心的一部分渴望倾诉，希望世界能看到真实的我们。

sentences.en: And there is a part of us that sees how people are brought down by scandal and gossip.
sentences.zh: 而另一部分则看到了人们是如何被丑闻和流言蜚语毁掉的。

sentences.en: And a cautious voice inside us says,
sentences.zh: 我们内心的那个谨慎的声音在说：

sentences.en: Be smart.
sentences.zh: 机灵点。

sentences.en: Keep your mouth shut.
sentences.zh: 闭紧你的嘴。

sentences.en: In today's show and our episode next week, and also in a special episode of Hidden Brain Plus,
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目、我们下周的节目，以及《隐藏的大脑》Plus特别节目中，

sentences.en: we explore the psychological costs and benefits of self-concealment and self-disclosure.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨自我隐藏和自我袒露的心理成本与收益。

sentences.en: Keeping Secrets, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 《保守秘密》，本周《隐藏的大脑》为您播出。

sentences.en: In the course of a day, countless thoughts and feelings enter our minds.
sentences.zh: 在一天当中，无数的想法和情感涌入我们的脑海。

sentences.en: We share some of these thoughts and feelings with others, but we keep most of them to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们会与他人分享其中一部分想法和情感，但大部分都留给了自己。

sentences.en: When is it smart to share?
sentences.zh: 什么时候分享是明智的？

sentences.en: When is it smart to hide?
sentences.zh: 什么时候隐瞒是明智的？

sentences.en: Is there scientific evidence that can guide us on what we should do?
sentences.zh: 有没有科学证据能指导我们该怎么做？

sentences.en: At Harvard University, psychologist Leslie John has spent many years studying these questions.
sentences.zh: 在哈佛大学，心理学家莱斯利·约翰花了很多年时间研究这些问题。

sentences.en: Leslie John, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 莱斯利·约翰，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Leslie, one of your favorite TV programs is the British comedy series, Mr. Bean.
sentences.zh: 莱斯利，你最喜欢的电视节目之一是英国喜剧《憨豆先生》。

sentences.en: There's one particular episode that you enjoy.
sentences.zh: 其中有一个情节你特别喜欢。

sentences.en: And for people who are unfamiliar with the show, who is Mr. Bean and what is he doing in this scene?
sentences.zh: 对于不熟悉这部剧的观众来说，憨豆先生是谁？他在这个场景里干了什么？

sentences.en: I love Mr. Bean.
sentences.zh: 我超爱憨豆先生。

sentences.en: Mr. Bean is a comic mime, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得憨豆先生是一个喜剧哑剧演员。

sentences.en: And his sweet spot is he finds these very relatable human situations, these quandaries we get ourselves in.
sentences.zh: 他的拿手好戏是捕捉那些极具共鸣的人类日常情境，也就是我们常常陷入的困境。

sentences.en: And then he comes up with absurd, almost childlike solutions.
sentences.zh: 然后他会想出荒诞的、近乎孩子气的解决方法。

sentences.en: So it's a really, really endearing and hilarious show.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一部非常非常讨人喜欢、令人捧腹的剧。

sentences.en: And also brings me back to my childhood because my father and I are the jokers of the family and we're huge Mr. Bean fans.
sentences.zh: 这也勾起了我的童年回忆，因为我和我父亲是家里的活宝，而且我们都是憨豆先生的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: So in this particular little sketch, Mr. Bean goes to a fancy schmancy restaurant and orders steak tartare, doesn't realize that that's essentially raw meat.
sentences.zh: 在这个特定的搞笑片段中，憨豆先生去了一家极其高级的餐厅点了一份鞑靼牛排，却不知道那基本上是生肉。

sentences.en: And so the waiter comes out with his meal with great flair, opens up the silver cloche that's on top of the plate.
sentences.zh: 于是服务员仪态优雅地端着餐点出来，打开了盘子上面的银色盖子。

sentences.en: And to Mr. Bean's horror, like his face says it all.
sentences.zh: 在憨豆先生看来，简直像是一场噩梦，他的表情说明了一切。

sentences.en: He's completely aghaSt.
sentences.zh: 他彻底惊呆了。

sentences.en: What have I done?
sentences.zh: 我都干了些什么？

sentences.en: But yet the waiter, you know, the waiter, of course, asks, how's it doing?
sentences.zh: 然而服务员，你知道的，服务员当然会问：感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: Is everything all right, sir?
sentences.zh: 一切都还好吧，先生？

sentences.en: And Mr. Bean does this, like his smiley, oh yes, everything is great.
sentences.zh: 而憨豆先生就这样，露出一脸假笑，哦，是的，一切都很好。

sentences.en: Oh yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: And then the waiter leaves and then what Mr. Bean proceeds to do is grab little dollops of the steak, of the raw meat, and put it wherever he can to get rid of it.
sentences.zh: 然后服务员走了，接着憨豆先生就开始抓起一小团一小团的生牛肉，能塞到哪儿就塞到哪儿，好把它们处理掉。

sentences.en: Because you have to follow through with the lie, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你得把这场谎言演下去，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to show progress on eating it.
sentences.zh: 你得装出有在吃的样子。

sentences.en: But so, yeah, so he like puts a little bit in the vase and then he leans back and he puts a little bit in the woman's purse behind him.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，他把一小块放进花瓶里，然后往后一靠，又把一小块放进身后女人的钱包里。

sentences.en: He hollows out, he hollows out a dinner roll and shoves it in.
sentences.zh: 他掏空了一个餐包，把肉塞了进去。

sentences.en: And then, then he even takes a dollop, sticks it directly on the table and sticks the plate to it like cement.
sentences.zh: 然后，他甚至还抓了一团，直接粘在桌子上，像水泥一样把盘子粘在上面。

sentences.en: So good.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I understand that you had your own Mr. Bean moment some years ago.
sentences.zh: 我听说你几年前也有过自己的“憨豆时刻”。

sentences.en: Can you set the scene for me and tell me what happened?
sentences.zh: 你能为我还原一下当时的场景，并告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I was a baby academic and I was invited out to give a talk at Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 好的，当时我还是个学术界的菜鸟，受邀去伯克利做个演讲。

sentences.en: So, totally swoon-worthy place.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个让人怦然心动的地方。

sentences.en: And two superstar scholars invited me out, they're married, and they invited me out to their house for dinner after the day.
sentences.zh: 两位超级巨星级的学者邀请了我，他们是一对夫妻，演讲结束后还邀请我去他们家共进晚餐。

sentences.en: And so, here I am, this googly-eyed junior academic, walking through the Berkeley Hills, walking to their house.
sentences.zh: 于是，我这个没见过世面的青年学者，走在伯克利的群山间，向他们家走去。

sentences.en: I get there and they open the door and they say, oh, we are so excited you're here.
sentences.zh: 我到了那里，他们打开门说，哦，你来我们太兴奋了。

sentences.en: We went to the market today and we're making steak tartare.
sentences.zh: 我们今天去了市场，正在做鞑靼牛排。

sentences.en: It's our favorite.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的最爱。

sentences.en: It's so special.
sentences.zh: 特别有意义。

sentences.en: And we only want to do the most special things for you.
sentences.zh: 我们只想为你做最特别的事情。

sentences.en: So, they laid it on thick.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们把牛排说得天花乱坠。

sentences.en: And, yeah, so I was like, oh, my gosh, I want to be Mr. Bean right now.
sentences.zh: 然后，我就在心里想：天哪，我此刻就想变成憨豆先生。

sentences.en: I want to do what he does.
sentences.zh: 我想做他做的事。

sentences.en: But, obviously, I couldn't.
sentences.zh: 但显然，我不能。

sentences.en: So, I pretended.
sentences.zh: 所以，我只能假装。

sentences.en: I was too ashamed, embarrassed, trying to make a good impression, trying to pretend I like highfalutin things.
sentences.zh: 我太羞愧了，感到尴尬，只想留下一个好印象，试图假装我喜欢那些高雅的东西。

sentences.en: And I ate it.
sentences.zh: 然后我把它吃下去了。

sentences.en: I got through it.
sentences.zh: 我总算挺过来了。

sentences.en: In fact, I've never told them this.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我从来没有告诉过他们这件事。

sentences.en: So, maybe they'll hear this and we'll have a good laugh over it.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许他们听到这个节目后，我们会为此开怀大笑吧。

sentences.en: But, yeah, that was my Mr. Bean moment.
sentences.zh: 总之，这就是我的“憨豆时刻”。

sentences.en: So, concealment can sometimes have bigger consequences, Leslie.
sentences.zh: 所以，隐瞒有时会带来更大的后果，莱斯利。

sentences.en: You tell the story of two women you know.
sentences.zh: 你讲过你认识的两个女人的故事。

sentences.en: You call them Jennifer and Donna.
sentences.zh: 你叫她们詹妮弗和唐娜。

sentences.en: When the story starts, Jennifer is preparing for an important event in her life.
sentences.zh: 故事开始时，詹妮弗正在为她人生中的一个重要事件做准备。

sentences.en: Paint a picture of the scene for me, Leslie.
sentences.zh: 莱斯利，能为我描绘一下当时的场景吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so, Jennifer was about 28 years old.
sentences.zh: 好的，詹妮弗当时大约28岁。

sentences.en: And she was on the cusp of a major life milestone.
sentences.zh: 她正处于人生一个重大里程碑的边缘。

sentences.en: The next month, she was slated to marry her betrothed, her fiancé, Philip.
sentences.zh: 下个月，她就要嫁给她相爱的人、她的未婚夫菲利普了。

sentences.en: The only thing was that she was starting to get these kind of nagging thoughts, these nagging doubts.
sentences.zh: 唯一的问题是，她开始产生这种纠缠不休的想法，这些挥之不去的疑虑。

sentences.en: And she didn't know, are these just like normal wedding jitters?
sentences.zh: 她不知道，这只是正常的婚前焦虑吗？

sentences.en: Is that a thing?
sentences.zh: 真有这种说法吗？

sentences.en: Or is this something I should pay more attention to?
sentences.zh: 还是说这是我应该多加关注的问题？

sentences.en: So, she was really close with her mother, Donna.
sentences.zh: 她和母亲唐娜关系非常亲密。

sentences.en: And she decided to give her mom a call.
sentences.zh: 于是她决定给妈妈打个电话。

sentences.en: And so, as the phone rings, Jennifer is transported back to her childhood home where her parents still lived.
sentences.zh: 电话铃响时，詹妮弗仿佛回到了父母至今仍居住的童年老宅。

sentences.en: And, you know, she's thinking about the living room where she and her brothers would do WWF wrestling matches.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她想起了客厅，她和哥哥们曾在那里进行世界摔角娱乐（WWF）比赛。

sentences.en: And then she thinks about the den where she envisions her mom to be at that time, sitting cozied up in the den with its faux wood paneling walls and all.
sentences.zh: 然后她想到了书房，她脑海中浮现出母亲当时的样子，舒舒服服地坐在贴着仿木镶板墙壁的书房里。

sentences.en: And then suddenly, hello?
sentences.zh: 接着，电话那头突然传来一声：喂？

sentences.en: And Jennifer says, hi, mom.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗说：嗨，妈妈。

sentences.en: It's me.
sentences.zh: 是我。

sentences.en: Donna immediately senses something's up and says, what's up, my chick?
sentences.zh: 唐娜立刻察觉到不对劲，说道：怎么啦，我的小宝贝？

sentences.en: And then Jennifer said to her mother, well, you know, I just, I don't know about these feelings I'm having.
sentences.zh: 然后詹妮弗对妈妈说：嗯，你知道的，我就是，我不知道自己这些感受是怎么回事。

sentences.en: And when I think about it, I really love Philip, but I love him like my best friend.
sentences.zh: 仔细想想，我真的很爱菲利普，但我对他的爱就像对最好的朋友一样。

sentences.en: And I don't know that I have, like, passionate love for him.
sentences.zh: 我不知道自己对他是那种充满激情的爱。

sentences.en: And I don't know, is that a problem?
sentences.zh: 我不知道这算不算是个问题？

sentences.en: Because I really love him in a best friend kind of way.
sentences.zh: 因为我对他的爱确实是挚友那种类型的。

sentences.en: And Donna listened.
sentences.zh: 唐娜静静地听着。

sentences.en: And then Jennifer said, mom, how did you know that you wanted to marry dad?
sentences.zh: 接着詹妮弗说：妈妈，你怎么知道自己想要嫁给爸爸的？

sentences.en: Because Jennifer always looked up to their marriage so much.
sentences.zh: 因为詹妮弗一直非常崇拜他们的婚姻。

sentences.en: They just seemed like they were amazing parents and they just seemed so happy.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来就像是出色的父母，而且显得非常幸福。

sentences.en: And that's all that Jennifer wanted was a really stable, loving, wonderful relationship.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗想要的就是一段真正稳定、充满爱意、美好的关系。

sentences.en: And her mom said, huh, it's funny, Jen, that you should ask because a month before I married your father, I was actually having similar doubts.
sentences.zh: 她妈妈说：啊，真搞笑，珍，你竟然会这么问，因为在我嫁给你父亲前的一个月，我其实也有过类似的疑虑。

sentences.en: And, oh, I'm so glad I went ahead with Miriam because look how happy we are.
sentences.zh: 而且，哦，我太高兴我最终还是决定结婚了，看看我们现在多幸福。

sentences.en: Look at how great our marriage is.
sentences.zh: 看看我们的婚姻有多好。

sentences.en: We work.
sentences.zh: 我们很合拍。

sentences.en: And she said, like, Jen, I know you.
sentences.zh: 她还说：珍，我了解你。

sentences.en: You're like me.
sentences.zh: 你跟我一样。

sentences.en: You struggle to make decisions.
sentences.zh: 你做决定很纠结。

sentences.en: You ruminate.
sentences.zh: 你总是反反复复地琢磨。

sentences.en: You question everything.
sentences.zh: 你对什么都要打个问号。

sentences.en: But sometimes you just, if it feels right, you got to go with it.
sentences.zh: 但有时你只要觉得感觉对了，就得顺其自然。

sentences.en: And so Jennifer took a lot of comfort in that phone call.
sentences.zh: 因此，这个电话给了詹妮弗极大的安慰。

sentences.en: And what she thought was, yeah, I already have, my love with Philip is already the mature kind.
sentences.zh: 她当时想的是：没错，我已经拥有了，我对菲利普的爱已经是成熟的爱了。

sentences.en: You know, passionate love fades.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，充满激情的爱会消逝。

sentences.en: What's really special and important is the mature kind, the kind that my mother has always had with my father.
sentences.zh: 真正特别和重要的是成熟的爱，也就是我母亲和父亲一直以来拥有的那种爱。

sentences.en: And so a month later, Jennifer and Philip were married.
sentences.zh: 于是一个月后，詹妮弗和菲利普结婚了。

sentences.en: And five very complicated years later, they were divorced.
sentences.zh: 而在经历了艰难的五年之后，他们离婚了。

sentences.en: So sometime after her divorce, Jennifer's brother sends her an email that changes everything.
sentences.zh: 所以在离婚后的某个时间，詹妮弗的哥哥给她发了一封改变一切的电子邮件。

sentences.en: What's in this email, Leslie?
sentences.zh: 这封邮件里写了什么，莱斯利？

sentences.en: It was an email chain that originated between Donna and her husband.
sentences.zh: 那是一封最初在唐娜和她丈夫之间发出的邮件链。

sentences.en: So it was a private between the two of them.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他们两个人之间的私密邮件。

sentences.en: And they ended up, what they started talking about was a very private, sensitive thing.
sentences.zh: 他们最终谈论的是一件非常私密、敏感的事情。

sentences.en: But where they ended up in the email chain was talking about finances.
sentences.zh: 但邮件链的最后，他们聊到了财务问题。

sentences.en: And they brought Jennifer's brother.
sentences.zh: 他们把詹妮弗的哥哥也扯了进来。

sentences.en: At this point, they added the brother to the email chain because the brother took care of their finances.
sentences.zh: 此时，他们把哥哥加进了邮件链，因为哥哥负责打理他们的财务。

sentences.en: And so then the brother forwards this to Jennifer.
sentences.zh: 接着，哥哥把这封邮件转发给了詹妮弗。

sentences.en: So Jennifer's sitting down in her bachelorette patch.
sentences.zh: 当时詹妮弗正坐在她的单身公寓里。

sentences.en: She's got her lovely coffee in the morning.
sentences.zh: 早上正喝着她美味的咖啡。

sentences.en: She's sitting down.
sentences.zh: 她坐了下来。

sentences.en: She opens her inbox.
sentences.zh: 她打开收件箱。

sentences.en: And she gets this email from her brother.
sentences.zh: 收到了她哥哥发来的这封邮件。

sentences.en: Hey, Jen, check this out.
sentences.zh: 嘿，珍，快看看这个。

sentences.en: Seems like they forgot what was at the beginning of the chain.
sentences.zh: 看来他们忘了这封邮件最初是关于什么的了。

sentences.en: And so, of course, Jennifer quickly scrolls, scrolls down, down, down.
sentences.zh: 所以，詹妮弗当然很快地往下、往下、往下滚动屏幕。

sentences.en: And wow, what she found out, she can never unknow.
sentences.zh: 天哪，她发现的内容是她永远无法当作没看到的。

sentences.en: And it's the kind of thing that is extremely shocking for someone to learn about their parents.
sentences.zh: 那是那种让任何人得知自己父母的事都会感到极其震惊的事情。

sentences.en: What the initial exchange revealed was that Donna and her husband had an unusual relationship.
sentences.zh: 最初的交流透露出，唐娜和她的丈夫拥有着一种不同寻常的关系。

sentences.en: It worked for them.
sentences.zh: 这种模式对他们而言很有效。

sentences.en: It was an open relationship of sorts.
sentences.zh: 那是一种某种意义上的开放式关系。

sentences.en: And they were discussing that in the chain in a very amicable way.
sentences.zh: 而且他们在邮件里非常心平气和地讨论着这件事。

sentences.en: Like, it was clear that it was a mutual agreement.
sentences.zh: 比如，很明显这是一个双方的共同协议。

sentences.en: And it was one that really worked for them.
sentences.zh: 而且对他们来说确实很管用。

sentences.en: And they even celebrated it, you could tell, in this email chain.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出来，他们甚至在这串电子邮件里庆祝了这件事。

sentences.en: So, I mean, Jennifer was a very open-minded person.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，珍妮弗是一个思想非常开放的人。

sentences.en: And she thought, wow, that's shocking.
sentences.zh: 她想，哇，这太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: But you do you.
sentences.zh: 但你还是做你自己吧。

sentences.en: And if that works for you, great.
sentences.zh: 如果这招对你管用，那就太好了。

sentences.en: But the more dominant feeling that Jennifer had, her whole body filled with anger and rage.
sentences.zh: 但珍妮弗内心最占上风的感觉是，她全身都充满了愤怒和狂怒。

sentences.en: Like, you know when you feel it super viscerally?
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道那种发自内心的深切感受吗？

sentences.en: That is how Jennifer felt.
sentences.zh: 这就是珍妮弗当时的感受。

sentences.en: Because immediately, she goes back in time in her mind to that fateful call that was, you know, seven or so years ago between her mother, Donna, and herself,
sentences.zh: 因为她脑海里立刻回想起大约七年前她和母亲唐娜之间那个命运般的电话，

sentences.en: the pre-wedding jitters call.
sentences.zh: 那个婚前焦虑电话。

sentences.en: And how Jennifer had felt so assuaged.
sentences.zh: 以及珍妮弗当时是如何感到如此宽慰的。

sentences.en: And Jennifer felt that Donna's words really, really did affect that decision.
sentences.zh: 珍妮弗觉得唐娜的话确实对那个决定产生了重大影响。

sentences.en: And the reason Jennifer was filled with rage because she said to herself, wait, mom, you only told me half the truth.
sentences.zh: 珍妮弗之所以充满愤怒，是因为她对自己说，等等，妈妈，你只告诉我了一半的事实。

sentences.en: You didn't tell me that the way your kind of escape valve, the way you handle this fact that you have people that you, shall I say,
sentences.zh: 你没有告诉我，你那种宣泄的途径——你处理身边那些人的方式，请容许我说，

sentences.en: enjoy your flirtations with maybe more than her father, was by having this release valve, this mutual agreement.
sentences.zh: 你可能比对她父亲更享受与他们调情——就是通过这种释放阀，这种共同的协议。

sentences.en: And this would have been extremely pertinent for Jennifer to have known because Jennifer was quite certain at that time that if she had known the full picture of what her parents' relationship was,
sentences.zh: 对于珍妮弗来说，知道这一点极其重要，因为珍妮弗当时非常确信，如果她知道父母关系的全部真相，

sentences.en: she would not have married Philip because she knew that although that worked for them, she knew it wouldn't work for her and that's not what she wanted.
sentences.zh: 她就不会嫁给菲利普，因为她知道虽然那对他们管用，但对她不管用，那也不是她想要的。

sentences.en: And so she really felt like, um, kind of betrayed by her mother.
sentences.zh: 所以她真的觉得自己被母亲背叛了。

sentences.en: And she felt like it would have been better if her mother had said nothing, if her mother hadn't even picked up the phone, than to share only half the story.
sentences.zh: 她觉得如果母亲什么都不说，甚至连电话都没打，也比只分享一半的故事要好。

sentences.en: Yeah, because Jennifer in some ways got comfort from what her mother was saying,
sentences.zh: 是的，因为珍妮弗在某种程度上从她母亲说的话中得到了安慰，

sentences.en: but her mother in some ways was not sharing that the terms of her relationship with her husband involved seeing other people.
sentences.zh: 但她母亲在某种程度上却没有透露她和丈夫关系中包括与其他人约会这一条款。

sentences.en: And there was, as you say, a release valve in this, in this marriage.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，在这段婚姻中有一个释放阀。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Did Jennifer ever confront Donna about what she had said previously?
sentences.zh: 珍妮弗有没有找过唐娜质问她以前说过的话？

sentences.en: Yes, she did.
sentences.zh: 是的，她找过。

sentences.en: Um, so years later, Jennifer, her anger faded because everything turned out beautifully for her.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以多年后，珍妮弗的愤怒消退了，因为一切对她来说结果都美极了。

sentences.en: She, she married the man of her dream.
sentences.zh: 她嫁给了她梦寐以求的男人。

sentences.en: She married her Prince Charming, who was, she was attracted to in all ways.
sentences.zh: 她嫁给了她的白马王子，一个她在各方面都被他吸引的人。

sentences.en: They had two beautiful children.
sentences.zh: 他们有了两个可爱的孩子。

sentences.en: Like, she was just living a slice of paradise.
sentences.zh: 就像，她简直生活在一片人间天堂里。

sentences.en: She was so happy, which made it easier for the old wounds to kind of heal.
sentences.zh: 她太幸福了，这让旧伤口更容易愈合。

sentences.en: But they were replaced by curiosity and wanting to learn more.
sentences.zh: 但它们被好奇心和想要了解更多的渴望所取代。

sentences.en: How did this start?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么开始的？

sentences.en: Why did it start?
sentences.zh: 为什么要开始？

sentences.en: Is it ever complicated?
sentences.zh: 这其中会不会很复杂？

sentences.en: So, one day, Grandma Donna was visiting and Jennifer's husband was, husband was out of town.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一天，唐娜外婆来做客，珍妮弗的丈夫出城了。

sentences.en: So Jennifer's like, this is like, she had a good workout during the day.
sentences.zh: 所以珍妮弗心想，这就好比，她白天刚进行了一场很好的锻炼。

sentences.en: She's like, I can do this.
sentences.zh: 她心想，我能行。

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 干吧。

sentences.en: And after dinner, pours two, two large, large glasses of scotch.
sentences.zh: 晚饭后，她倒了两大杯苏格兰威士忌。

sentences.en: There is such a thing as liquid courage.
sentences.zh: 世上确实有借酒壮胆这回事。

sentences.en: Sits down with her mom and says, do you remember that phone call we had before my first marriage?
sentences.zh: 她和妈妈坐下来，说道，你还记得我第一次结婚前我们打的那通电话吗？

sentences.en: And Donna said, like, a wave of warmth, like, motherly warmth smile came across her face.
sentences.zh: 唐娜说，脸上泛起了一股温暖的涟漪，母亲般的温暖微笑。

sentences.en: And she said, yeah, I do.
sentences.zh: 她说，记得，我当然记得。

sentences.en: And I've often wondered whether I said the right thing.
sentences.zh: 我经常纳闷自己当时有没有说对话。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And that was just the perfect segue in.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个完美的切入点。

sentences.en: And then what preceded was probably the most meaningful conversation Jennifer had had definitely with her mother, potentially with anyone ever.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是珍妮弗一生中——绝对是跟她母亲，也可能跟任何人——有过最有意义的一次谈话。

sentences.en: And so that just really, really ended up deep in their relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以这最终真的大大加深了他们的关系。

sentences.en: All of us make choices in nearly every moment of our lives about what to share with others and what to keep private.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎在生活的每一个时刻都在做出选择，决定与他人分享什么，又对什么保持隐私。

sentences.en: These decisions have consequences for our health, our well-being and our relationships.
sentences.zh: 这些决定对我们的健康、幸福和人际关系都会产生影响。

sentences.en: When we come back, the psychology of self-concealment.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将探讨自我隐瞒的心理学。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Leslie John is a psychologist at Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 莱斯莉·约翰是哈佛商学院的一位心理学家。

sentences.en: She studies self-concealment and self-disclosure.
sentences.zh: 她专门研究自我隐瞒和自我披露。

sentences.en: Leslie, most of us are keenly aware of the dangers of oversharing.
sentences.zh: 莱斯莉，我们大多数人都对过度分享的危险有着敏锐的意识。

sentences.en: We've all heard stories about someone who, you know, posted a photo of themselves at a drunken frat party and then they got turned down for a job years later.
sentences.zh: 我们都听说过这样的故事：某人在一个喝醉酒的兄弟会派对上拍了张照片并发布出去，结果几年后找工作时遭到拒绝。

sentences.en: Talk for a moment about this.
sentences.zh: 能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Our default position is often, when in doubt, say nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们的默认立场往往是，如果心存疑虑，那就什么也别说。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You can think of even those sayings from wartime.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以联想起战争时期的那些名言。

sentences.en: Loose lips sink ships, right?
sentences.zh: 祸从口出，对吧？

sentences.en: It feels like the default, the strong default we have is to stay silent if there's any doubt.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们的默认原则——我们坚定的默认原则是，如果有任何疑问，就保持沉默。

sentences.en: And to your point, I mean, the public discourse is kind of obsessed with TMI moments, right?
sentences.zh: 而且正如你所说，公众舆论有点痴迷于“TMI”（信息过载）时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: Of outing people.
sentences.zh: 把人曝光。

sentences.en: That's TMI.
sentences.zh: 那是信息过载。

sentences.en: That's oversharing.
sentences.zh: 那是过度分享。

sentences.en: And it is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Of course, we can share too much at the wrong time with the wrong people.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们可能会在错误的时间向错误的人分享太多信息。

sentences.en: It can bite us in all these ways.
sentences.zh: 这会在各个方面反噬我们。

sentences.en: But what I found in our research is that we don't pay attention, we don't pay enough attention to the other side of the coin, which is what I call TLI, too little information.
sentences.zh: 但在我们的研究中，我发现我们没有给予足够关注的是硬币的另一面，也就是我所说的“TLI”，即信息过少。

sentences.en: And that there are very real harms to not opening up, to staying silent.
sentences.zh: 不敞开心扉、保持沉默会带来非常现实的危害。

sentences.en: And so I'm hoping that we can start adjudicating these decisions of whether to share or not in a more balanced, even-handed way where we consider both TMI and TLI.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望我们能开始以一种更平衡、更公正的方式来裁决这些是否分享的决定，既要考虑TMI，也要考虑TLI。

sentences.en: Let's look at some of the ways in which concealment can hurt us.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看隐瞒可能伤害我们的几种方式。

sentences.en: You've talked about some shocking research into how much information people hide from their own doctors.
sentences.zh: 你曾谈到过一些令人震惊的研究，关于人们对自己的医生隐瞒了多少信息。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: So there's some fascinating research by some scholars in the medical area where they have asked, interviewed patients, essentially,
sentences.zh: 医学领域的一些学者做了一些非常有趣的研究，他们基本上是通过询问和采访患者，

sentences.en: whether they've hid some really pertinent health information from their doctor, right?
sentences.zh: 看他们是否对医生隐瞒了一些非常相关的健康信息，对吧？

sentences.en: The very person who has taken an oath to protect them.
sentences.zh: 而这个人正是发誓要保护他们的人。

sentences.en: And it's 80% of people admit to not being forthcoming, to hiding something from their physicians.
sentences.zh: 结果有80%的人承认自己没有全盘托出，对医生有所隐瞒。

sentences.en: And it's super relatable, right?
sentences.zh: 这超级能引发共鸣，对吧？

sentences.en: But it's also bananas on another hand, right?
sentences.zh: 但从另一方面来看，这也太离谱了，对吧？

sentences.en: Because this person could help you.
sentences.zh: 因为这个人本可以帮到你。

sentences.en: But it's understandable because health stuff is often so sensitive.
sentences.zh: 但这也情有可原，因为健康问题往往非常敏感。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, someone is, you know, trying to quit smoking, for example, and their doctor has been urging them to quit smoking for a number of years.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，比方说有人正试图戒烟，他们的医生多年来一直敦促他们戒烟。

sentences.en: But they've, in fact, been sneaking a couple of cigarettes or they're trying to drink a little less.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，他们一直在偷偷抽几支烟，或者试图少喝一点酒。

sentences.en: But they haven't been successful.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有成功。

sentences.en: It's hard to come clean and tell your doctor, this is what's actually going on in my life.
sentences.zh: 要向医生坦白并说“这就是我生活中实际发生的事情”是很艰难的。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I had this really funny moment in college where I went to the clinic to get it.
sentences.zh: 我在大学里有过这样一件非常搞笑的事，当时我去诊所看病。

sentences.en: I wanted an STD teSt.
sentences.zh: 我想做个性病检测。

sentences.en: And I get to the clinic and I was so impressed because when you get there, they let you write down what your issue is.
sentences.zh: 我到了诊所，印象非常深刻，因为当你到那儿时，他们让你写下你的问题。

sentences.en: So you never have to say the words out loud.
sentences.zh: 所以你永远不必大声说出那些字眼。

sentences.en: So I wrote it down on the sheet of paper.
sentences.zh: 于是我把它写在了一张纸上。

sentences.en: I handed it in.
sentences.zh: 我把它交了上去。

sentences.en: But then when it was my turn, this is like a Larry David episode.
sentences.zh: 但轮到我的时候，这就像是《抑制热情》里的情节。

sentences.en: When it was my turn, the nurse said, Leslie John, STD testing.
sentences.zh: 轮到我时，护士说：“莱斯莉·约翰，性病检测。”

sentences.en: Nightmare.
sentences.zh: 简直是噩梦。

sentences.en: You tell the story of a physician named John Cullen, who was literally about to cut open a patient to take out their appendix,
sentences.zh: 你讲过一个名叫约翰·库伦的医生的故事，他当时正准备剖开一个病人的腹部来割除阑尾，

sentences.en: but then realized that the patient may, in fact, not have appendicitis after all.
sentences.zh: 结果却发现这个病人可能根本不是阑尾炎。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This is the, like, a super grand poobah in the American Academy of Family Physicians president, Dr. John Cullen.
sentences.zh: 这位是美国美国家庭医师学会的主席，简直是个超级大人物，约翰·库伦医生。

sentences.en: Maybe that's what made it a little bit harder, actually, because he was so high status.
sentences.zh: 也许正因如此，事情变得更艰难了一点，因为他的地位太高了。

sentences.en: At any rate, he was literally about to cut open a patient to take out their appendix.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他当时确实正准备剖开一个病人的腹部来切除阑尾。

sentences.en: But he had this kind of sixth sense that something, you know, you do enough reps of these things and you get a sixth sense and something wasn't right.
sentences.zh: 但他有一种第六感，觉得有些不对劲——你知道的，这种手术做多了，你就会有一种第六感，觉得哪里不对劲。

sentences.en: And apparently, symptoms of drug abuse, specifically methamphetamines, they can actually resemble those of appendicitis.
sentences.zh: 显然，吸毒过量的症状，特别是冰毒，实际上可能与阑尾炎的症状相似。

sentences.en: And so before he cut her open, Dr. Cullen gave it one final chance.
sentences.zh: 所以在切开她的肚子之前，库伦医生给了最后一次机会。

sentences.en: He said, I quote, we're about to cut you open here.
sentences.zh: 他说，我原话引述：“我们马上就要动手术切开你了。”

sentences.en: Are you sure you don't want to tell me anything else?
sentences.zh: “你确定没有什么别的要告诉我吗？”

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Finally, the patient fessed up and the surgery was aborted.
sentences.zh: 最终，病人招了，手术取消了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of incredible, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直太不可思议了，对吧？

sentences.en: People are willing to have themselves cut open instead of revealing something that they think is shameful.
sentences.zh: 宁愿让自己被开刀剖腹，也不愿意透露一件他们认为羞耻的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You also tell another hospital story, this one involving a patient who was bleeding uncontrollably during surgery.
sentences.zh: 你还讲了另一个医院的故事，讲的是一个病人在手术过程中流血不止。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This one's even more shocking because it was a life-threatening situation.
sentences.zh: 这个故事更加震撼，因为这是一个危及生命的状况。

sentences.en: So before the surgery, the surgeon asks the patient, you know, are you taking any medications?
sentences.zh: 所以在手术前，外科医生问病人：“你知道，你在服用什么药物吗？”

sentences.en: And the patient says no.
sentences.zh: 病人说没有。

sentences.en: And then the surgeon comes out to the waiting room just before he's about to operate and says to the mom, are you sure she's not taking anything?
sentences.zh: 然后就在准备动手术之前，外科医生走到候诊室对妈妈说：“你确定她没在吃什么药吗？”

sentences.en: Again, the surgeon had kind of a sixth sense.
sentences.zh: 同样，这位外科医生也有某种第六感。

sentences.en: And then the mother said, nope, nothing.
sentences.zh: 然后母亲说：“没有，什么都没有。”

sentences.en: Finally, the surgeon asked again and is imploring her to be honest, please, please, this is your daughter's life.
sentences.zh: 最后，外科医生再次询问，恳求她实话实说：“求求你，求求你，这可是你女儿的命。”

sentences.en: And finally, and it wasn't even the daughter that revealed this.
sentences.zh: 最后——甚至都不是女儿自己透露的。

sentences.en: It was her mother that finally revealed that the child, the daughter, the grown daughter was taking weight loss supplements, but of course was too ashamed to say so.
sentences.zh: 是她的母亲最终透露，这个孩子、这个女儿、这个已经成年的女儿一直在服用减肥补充剂，但当然是因为太羞于启齿而没有说出来。

sentences.en: And I guess that interferes with bleeding or something.
sentences.zh: 我猜这会干扰凝血机制还是怎么的。

sentences.en: And that literally saved her life.
sentences.zh: 这简直是救了她一命。

sentences.en: The surgeon ran back in.
sentences.zh: 外科医生赶紧跑了回去。

sentences.en: It was that serious.
sentences.zh: 情况就是这么严重。

sentences.en: So it's really, it's very real, the shame we feel around opening up, the apprehension, the worry that someone's going to judge us is a very, very real concern.
sentences.zh: 所以这是非常真实的，我们对于敞开心扉感到的羞耻、忧虑，以及担心别人会评判我们的担忧，是一个非常非常现实的问题。

sentences.en: Because look at the lengths people go to to avoid it.
sentences.zh: 因为看看人们为了避免这种情况会付出多大的代价。

sentences.en: Besides complicating our medical care when we don't share things with our doctors, I understand there's research showing that secrecy negatively affects our immune functioning?
sentences.zh: 除了在我们不对医生坦白时使我们的医疗护理变得复杂之外，据我所知，还有研究表明保守秘密会对我们的免疫功能产生负面影响？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When you keep a secret, one of the tricky things is that your mind is very active.
sentences.zh: 当你保守秘密时，棘手的事情之一就是你的大脑非常活跃。

sentences.en: Keeping a secret is not an inner activity.
sentences.zh: 保守秘密可不是一项内在的活动。

sentences.en: It's not a neutral thing.
sentences.zh: 它不是一件中性的事。

sentences.en: Yet we often think that that's a neutral thing, right?
sentences.zh: 然而我们经常认为这是一件中性的事，对吧？

sentences.en: We think that not sharing is neutral.
sentences.zh: 我们认为不分享是中性的。

sentences.en: But in fact, it can be an incredibly active process.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这可能是一个极其活跃的过程。

sentences.en: So when you keep a secret, think about keeping a secret.
sentences.zh: 所以当你保守秘密时，想想保守秘密这件事。

sentences.en: You have to constantly monitor, right?
sentences.zh: 你必须时刻监控，对吧？

sentences.en: When you're in a conversation where it could be relevant, you got to be, you got to monitor your brain.
sentences.zh: 当你处于一段可能与此相关的谈话中时，你必须监控你的大脑。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then, and that's stressful.
sentences.zh: 然后，这会带来压力。

sentences.en: And so that like literally can increase your cortisol, your stress hormones.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的会增加你的皮质醇，也就是你的压力荷尔蒙。

sentences.en: It can affect you in this way.
sentences.zh: 它会以这种方式对你产生影响。

sentences.en: And it also, there have been lots of studies showing that when you are keeping a secret, you score lower on IQ tests because it literally preoccupies your brain.
sentences.zh: 而且还有很多研究表明，当你保守秘密时，你在智商测试中的得分会较低，因为这实实在在地占据了你的大脑。

sentences.en: It takes away brain space.
sentences.zh: 它占用了大脑的空间。

sentences.en: You talk about one of the costs of self-concealment is that it can keep us from forming relationships or deepening relationships.
sentences.zh: 你谈到自我隐瞒的代价之一是，它会阻止我们建立或加深人际关系。

sentences.en: You tell the story of a, perhaps a trivial encounter in an elevator when you were a young scholar on the job market.
sentences.zh: 你讲了一个故事，也许是你在求职市场上的年轻学者时期，在电梯里的一次微不足道的偶遇。

sentences.en: Tell me that story, Leslie.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲那个故事吧，莱斯利。

sentences.en: Yeah, so one of the things, the principles that's really important in new relationships, new friendships, new acquaintanceships, new romances is mutual self-disclosure.
sentences.zh: 好的，在新关系、新友谊、新熟人关系、新恋情中非常重要的原则之一就是相互自我披露。

sentences.en: It's like a ping pong pattern of reciprocity where you say something, the other person reciprocates with something just as deep.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种互惠的乒乓球模式，你说一些事，对方也会用同样深刻的事来回应。

sentences.en: You don't start super deep.
sentences.zh: 你们不会一开始就聊得非常深。

sentences.en: You start maybe on a more shallow, but then you go back and forth, ping pong back and forth, and you get increasingly more vulnerable with each other.
sentences.zh: 你们可能从比较表面的话题开始，然后来回切磋，像打乒乓球一样来回互动，彼此之间越来越敞开心扉。

sentences.en: This comes back to even Arthur Aaron's studies, right, the 36 questions where you get people to ask and answer questions to each other,
sentences.zh: 这甚至可以追溯到亚瑟·艾伦的研究，对吧，那36个问题，让人们互相提问和回答，

sentences.en: and that makes them like each other and forge friendships.
sentences.zh: 这能让他们互相产生好感并建立友谊。

sentences.en: And so this encounter, this is what I call a reciprocity fail.
sentences.zh: 所以这次偶遇，就是我所说的互惠失败。

sentences.en: When one person puts out an olive branch, they put themselves out there, and then they're shut down.
sentences.zh: 当一个人向对方抛出橄榄枝、展现自我时，却遭到了冷遇。

sentences.en: So what happened to me, I was trying to get an academic job.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时的经历是，我正试图找一份学术工作。

sentences.en: I was on that academic job market.
sentences.zh: 我当时在学术求职市场上。

sentences.en: I'm in my, like, Banana Republic black suit, which, fun fact, after the fact, I realized I still had the stitching and the double bent in the back.
sentences.zh: 我穿着香蕉共和国的黑色西装，有趣的是，事后我才发现，当时衣服背面居然还带着缝线和双层褶裥。

sentences.en: I hadn't unstitched it.
sentences.zh: 我还没拆掉线。

sentences.en: So rookie.
sentences.zh: 真是个新手。

sentences.en: So endearing.
sentences.zh: 太可爱了。

sentences.en: So in this rookie academic job market, what you do is there's a big hotel, and all the different universities that are recruiting, they rent out different suites.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种菜鸟学术求职市场上，你做的事就是会有一个大酒店，所有招聘的不同大学都会租下不同的套房。

sentences.en: And so every hour on the hour, there's this jamboree of rookie candidates moving from room to room to pitch themselves.
sentences.zh: 因此，每到整点，就会有一大群菜鸟候选人在各个房间之间穿梭，推销自己。

sentences.en: So I found myself in the elevator.
sentences.zh: 然后我发现自己进了电梯。

sentences.en: I get into the elevator, and there's one, clearly a job candidate in there.
sentences.zh: 我走进电梯，里面明显有一个求职候选人。

sentences.en: The elevator doors close.
sentences.zh: 电梯门关上了。

sentences.en: So we're literally in a steel vault.
sentences.zh: 所以我们真的在一个钢铁保险库里。

sentences.en: And I say, I let my guard down.
sentences.zh: 我说，我放松了警惕。

sentences.en: I just say, oh, I'm so exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，哦，我太累了。

sentences.en: My whole body just was, like, exuded exhaustion.
sentences.zh: 我的整个身体都散发着疲惫感。

sentences.en: And then what did the fellow job candidate do?
sentences.zh: 然后另一个求职候选人做了什么？

sentences.en: He straightened right up, and he said, oh, this is such an exciting and fun opportunity to get senior faculty to weigh in on all of my research.
sentences.zh: 他一下子挺直了腰板，说，哦，这是一个多么令人兴奋和有趣的机遇，能让资深教员对我的所有研究提出意见。

sentences.en: It's so amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: And then I, like, gave him the stink eye with my whole body.
sentences.zh: 然后我用全身向他翻了个白眼。

sentences.en: I just was, like, in my mind, what I thought is, like, really?
sentences.zh: 我当时脑子里想的是，真的吗？

sentences.en: We're literally in a steel vault, and you can't, we can't just be real, like, have a real moment of kind of shared feeling that would make us both feel more relaxed.
sentences.zh: 我们明明在一个钢铁保险库里，难道我们就不能真实一点吗？来一个真正能引起共鸣的时刻，让我们两个都感到更轻松。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's interesting, this idea that a reciprocity, the sting of a reciprocity failure lingers because we see each other regularly at conferences.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，互惠失败带来的刺痛感会挥之不去，因为我们经常在学术会议上见面。

sentences.en: He's very accomplished, and I'm sure he's a really nice guy.
sentences.zh: 他非常成功，而且我相信他真的是个很好的人。

sentences.en: But I've never felt the urge to, like, go chat him up.
sentences.zh: 但我从来没有过想去和他聊聊的冲动。

sentences.en: And I think I would attribute it to that.
sentences.zh: 我想这要归咎于那次经历。

sentences.en: In other words, you basically, you know, you put yourself out there.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，基本上你知道，你主动展现了自我。

sentences.en: He declined.
sentences.zh: 而他拒绝了。

sentences.en: And the point that you're making is not just that you didn't have an exchange in that elevator for 30 seconds,
sentences.zh: 你所要表达的重点不仅仅是你在电梯里没有进行30秒的交流，

sentences.en: but in some ways it's had ramifications.
sentences.zh: 而且在某种程度上，这产生了后续影响。

sentences.en: You know, it's echoed, if you will, down the years where you actually haven't tried to make a connection with it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它在岁月中回响，以至于你实际上再也没有尝试过去和他建立联系。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so imagine if we play the other route of, imagine if he had reciprocated and been like,
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，如果我们换一种方式，想象如果他给予了回应，并说：

sentences.en: I know, I just had this crazy interview.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我刚经历了这场疯狂的面试。

sentences.en: Can you believe it?
sentences.zh: 你敢相信吗？

sentences.en: This person said that, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 这个人说了那个，巴拉巴拉巴拉。

sentences.en: Like a moment, a moment like that.
sentences.zh: 就像这样一个时刻。

sentences.en: Imagine we could have been lifelong friends.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，我们本可以成为终身好友。

sentences.en: So many of us, I think, intuit that self-concealment has costs, Leslie.
sentences.zh: 我想我们中的许多人都凭直觉感到自我隐瞒是有代价的，莱斯利。

sentences.en: And many of us, I think, intuit what those costs are.
sentences.zh: 我想我们中的许多人也能直觉到这些代价是什么。

sentences.en: But one reason we hide is that we believe that we alone harbor shameful secrets.
sentences.zh: 但我们选择隐瞒的一个原因，是因为我们相信只有我们自己怀揣着见不得人的秘密。

sentences.en: Talk about this idea that when it comes to the things that we hold secret,
sentences.zh: 谈谈这个观点，当谈到我们保守的秘密时，

sentences.en: we somehow imagine that we are the only ones holding those secrets.
sentences.zh: 我们总觉得只有我们自己才藏着这些秘密。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think a big reason is that secrets are not visible.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得一个很大的原因在于秘密是看不见的。

sentences.en: We don't see all of the secrets that people are holding.
sentences.zh: 我们看不到其他人保守的所有秘密。

sentences.en: It makes us feel like we're the only ones that hold secrets,
sentences.zh: 这让我们觉得只有自己才怀揣秘密，

sentences.en: which makes them even more kind of clandestine, right?
sentences.zh: 从而让这些秘密显得更加见不得人，对吧？

sentences.en: And they take an even bigger toll on this.
sentences.zh: 并且它们为此付出了更大的代价。

sentences.en: It's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Michael Slepian over at Columbia has done, and Malia Mason,
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学的迈克尔·斯莱皮安（Michael Slepian）和玛丽亚·梅森（Malia Mason），

sentences.en: they've done some really great work on a questionnaire
sentences.zh: 他们围绕问卷调查做了一些非常出色的工作，

sentences.en: to find out what people's common secrets are.
sentences.zh: 旨在找出人们常见的秘密是什么。

sentences.en: And it turns out that there are lots of things that people tend to keep secret.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，人们往往会保守很多秘密。

sentences.en: It's a very normal thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非常正常的事。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if social media in some ways compounds this,
sentences.zh: 我在想，社交媒体在某种程度上是否加剧了这一点，

sentences.en: because now we not only don't hear our people's secrets,
sentences.zh: 因为现在我们不仅听不到别人的秘密，

sentences.en: but we're constantly being presented this view of other people's lives
sentences.zh: 而且我们不断地被呈现出其他人生活的景象，

sentences.en: that's always glamorous and excited and people having a great time at fancy restaurants.
sentences.zh: 总是那么光鲜亮丽、激动人心，人们在高级餐厅里玩得很开心。

sentences.en: And now we feel, well, clearly the fact that I'm eating a reheated dinner from three days ago,
sentences.zh: 于是我们现在觉得，很显然，我居然在吃三天前加热的剩饭，

sentences.en: it must show that I'm the only one who has this dirty secret.
sentences.zh: 这肯定说明我是唯一一个拥有这个肮脏秘密的人。

sentences.en: Everyone else is having a grand old time.
sentences.zh: 其他所有人都在过着无忧无虑的美好生活。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: Social media is so toxic for that reason.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，社交媒体才如此有毒。

sentences.en: It's exactly as you said.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说的那样。

sentences.en: People present a curated portrait of themselves.
sentences.zh: 人们展示的是自己经过精心修饰的形象。

sentences.en: And logically, we know this, but we cannot, we have a hard time correcting for it,
sentences.zh: 从逻辑上我们知道这一点，但我们做不到，我们很难去纠正这种本能的感觉。

sentences.en: the visceral feeling.
sentences.zh: 那种发自内心的感受。

sentences.en: You see someone who looks gorgeous with their perfect children and their perfect life,
sentences.zh: 当你看到一个看起来光鲜亮丽的人，带着完美的孩子和完美的生活，

sentences.en: and you think, oh my God, meanwhile, my children are screaming.
sentences.zh: 你就会想，天哪，与此同时我的孩子却在尖叫。

sentences.en: And so it makes you feel badly about yourself, these kinds of comparisons.
sentences.zh: 所以这种比较会让你对自己的感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: When we come back, Leslie comes up with a survey asking people
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，莱斯利提出了一项调查，询问人们

sentences.en: if they have ever cheated on their taxes, watched pornography,
sentences.zh: 是否曾在纳税上作假、看色情内容，

sentences.en: or called in sick when they wanted to spend a day at the beach.
sentences.zh: 或者在想去海滩玩一天时谎称生病请假。

sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Can you think of a secret you haven't shared with anyone?
sentences.zh: 你能想起一个你从未对任何人分享过的秘密吗？

sentences.en: How does keeping the secret make you feel?
sentences.zh: 保守这个秘密让你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: What do you think would happen if you shared the secret with others?
sentences.zh: 如果你把这个秘密分享给别人，你觉得会发生什么？

sentences.zh: 如果你愿意与《隐藏的大脑》听众分享你的个人故事，

sentences.en: please find a very quiet room and record a voice memo on your phone.
sentences.zh: 请找一个非常安静的房间，在手机上录下一段语音备忘录。

sentences.en: Two or three minutes is plenty.
sentences.zh: 两到三分钟就足够了。

sentences.zh: 将该文件通过电子邮件发送给我们：feedback@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.zh: 邮件主题请写：Secrets（秘密）。

sentences.zh: 再重复一遍，邮箱是 feedback@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Psychologist Leslie John is the author of Revealing,
sentences.zh: 心理学家莱斯利·约翰（Leslie John）是《过度分享的被低估力量》一书的作者。

sentences.en: The Underrated Power of Oversharing.
sentences.zh: 莱斯利，当你深入探讨尴尬披露的世界时，

sentences.en: Leslie, as you dived into the world of embarrassing disclosures,
sentences.zh: 你和一位导师曾设计过调查问题。

sentences.en: you and an advisor once came up with survey questions.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这是一项极具挑战性的练习。

sentences.en: This turned out to be a very challenging exercise.
sentences.zh: 怎么说呢？

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 我想我可能保持着最尴尬的博士生与导师对话的世界纪录。

sentences.en: I think I might hold the world record for the most awkward doctoral advisor-advisee conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以当我还是个博士生时，你知道的，我对

sentences.en: So when I was a doctoral student, you know, I've been interested in this topic of
sentences.zh: 揭露隐私、自我披露秘密这个话题已经感兴趣很长时间了。

sentences.en: revealing privacy, self-disclosure secrets for a very long time now.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我读博士时，我和我的导师合作设计了一系列调查，

sentences.en: And so when I was a doctoral student, I worked with my advisor to devise a series of surveys
sentences.zh: 我们在调查中问人们敏感的问题，并通过改变不同的变量来了解不同的事情。

sentences.en: where we asked people sensitive questions and we varied different things to learn different things.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要想出非常敏感的问题来问大家。

sentences.en: And so we needed to come up with really sensitive things to ask people.
sentences.zh: 于是我们坐在他的办公室里。

sentences.en: And so we sat in his office.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说是一个极其清晰的记忆。

sentences.en: It's one of these, like, flashbulb memories for me.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你清楚地记得自己当时穿了什么衣服，坐在哪里。

sentences.en: You know, you remember exactly what you were wearing and where you were seated.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他一上来就单刀直入。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he just starts with a bang.
sentences.zh: 他说，兽交怎么样？

sentences.en: He says, what about bestiality?
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我当时的心情就像是，我最想给留下好印象的人竟然说出了这句话。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, I was, like, the person that I'm most trying to impress said that.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: And so I was, like, what do I do?
sentences.zh: 在我头脑风暴提出的各种事情中，我要选择像那样超级敏感的话题吗？

sentences.en: Do I go for something super sensitive like that in the things that I bring to the table
sentences.zh: 我觉得我当时说的一切，都会让他觉得我是一个老古板。

sentences.en: brainstorming?
sentences.zh: 或者如果我说了一些真的很糟糕的事，比如，你有没有隐瞒过伴侣自己曾患有性病？

sentences.en: I felt like everything I said then was, like, maybe he's going to think I'm a prude.
sentences.zh: 那他就会觉得我很轻率。

sentences.en: Or then if I said something really bad, like, have you ever neglected to tell a partner about
sentences.zh: 仅仅一想到我还在为我的导师担心，天哪，

sentences.en: an STD you had?
sentences.zh: 这实在是太尴尬了。

sentences.en: Then he'd think I was reckless.
sentences.zh: 但我们挺过来了。

sentences.en: And just even the thought of that I am worrying about my advisor, like, it just, oh, gosh,
sentences.zh: 我们咬牙坚持了下来。

sentences.en: it was so cringy.
sentences.zh: 我们想出了一份绝佳的清单。

sentences.en: But we got through it.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，我一直在我的职业生涯中使用这些问题以及这些主题的各种变体。

sentences.en: We powered through.
sentences.zh: 所以这项调查采用的是以“你是否曾经”开头的问题形式。

sentences.en: And we came up with a great liSt.
sentences.zh: 我想请你宣读一下这些问题的清单，莱斯利。

sentences.en: And I've since been using those questions and variations on those themes for kind of
sentences.zh: 我希望听众们也扪心自问，他们是否做过其中的任何事情。

sentences.en: my career so far.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么，这些问题，嗯，请注意，如果你们身边有小孩的话，这些问题可都是重量级的。

sentences.en: So the survey took the form of questions that start with, have you ever?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾与朋友现任的丈夫、妻子或伴侣发生过性关系？

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you can read out a list of these questions, Leslie.
sentences.zh: 你是否曾幻想过做一些可怕的事情，例如虐待某人？

sentences.en: And I want listeners to ask themselves if they have ever done any of these things.
sentences.zh: 你是否曾偷过价值超过100美元的东西？

sentences.en: Okay, so, yeah, the questions, um, be warned, they're doozies if you have children around.
sentences.zh: 你是否曾观看过色情资料？

sentences.en: Have you ever had sex with the current husband, wife, or partner of a friend?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾提出过虚假的保险索赔？

sentences.en: Have you ever had a fantasy of doing something terrible, e.g. torturing to someone?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾在纳税申报单上作假？

sentences.en: Have you ever stolen anything worth more than $100?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾声称自己拥有实际上并未获得的学历？

sentences.en: Have you ever looked at pornographic material?
sentences.zh: 在恋爱关系中，你是否曾与伴侣以外的人调情？

sentences.en: Have you ever made a false insurance claim?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾将别人的工作成果据为己有？

sentences.en: Have you ever cheated on your tax return?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾在朋友喝得酩酊大醉后，仍然让他们开车？

sentences.en: Have you ever claimed to have education that you didn't actually have?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾向任何人谎报过你的收入？

sentences.en: While in a relationship, have you ever flirted with somebody other than your partner?
sentences.zh: 在恋爱关系中，你曾和伴侣以外的人调情过吗？

sentences.en: Have you ever taken credit for someone else's work?
sentences.zh: 你曾将别人的工作成果据为己有吗？

sentences.en: Have you ever let a friend drive after you thought he or she had had too much to drink?
sentences.zh: 你曾在一个朋友喝得太多时，还让他或她开车吗？

sentences.en: Have you ever lied about your income to someone?
sentences.zh: 你曾向任何人隐瞒过自己的真实收入吗？

sentences.en: Have you ever called in sick when you weren't sick?
sentences.zh: 你有没有在没生病的时候装病请过假？

sentences.en: Have you ever pretended not to see a beggar to avoid being seen as stingy?
sentences.zh: 你有没有为了避免被当成小气鬼而假装没看到乞丐？

sentences.en: Have you ever gone on a date only to make somebody else jealous?
sentences.zh: 你有没有为了让别人吃醋而去约会？

sentences.en: Have you ever drunk so much that you got a hangover?
sentences.zh: 你有没有喝到宿醉过？

sentences.en: Have you ever littered in a public space?
sentences.zh: 你有没有在公共场所乱扔过垃圾？

sentences.en: Have you ever failed to do chores in a shared house or apartment?
sentences.zh: 你有没有在合租或合住时没做好家务？

sentences.en: And have you ever failed to tip a waiter in a country in which tipping is customary?
sentences.zh: 在有给小费习惯的国家，你有没有没给服务员小费？

sentences.en: These are the questions.
sentences.zh: 这些就是问题所在。

sentences.en: And these, I've more or less said them in a decreasing order of sensitivity.
sentences.zh: 而且这些问题，我差不多是按敏感程度递减的顺序排列的。

sentences.en: I'm sure people must clam up if someone asked them this question in a research setting.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，如果在研究环境中问人们这个问题，大家一定会三缄其口。

sentences.en: That's what I would think too.
sentences.zh: 我也是这么想的。

sentences.en: But again and again, like across all of the research I've done,
sentences.zh: 但一次又一次，在我做过的所有研究中，

sentences.en: the one thing that really surprises me is how forthcoming people often are.
sentences.zh: 真正让我惊讶的是，人们往往是多么坦诚。

sentences.en: It almost seems like people really want to reveal.
sentences.zh: 这看起来简直像是人们真的渴望吐露心声。

sentences.en: And in fact, there's been subsequent research showing that we do have this kind of internal
sentences.zh: 事实上，后来的研究表明，我们的确有这种内在的

sentences.en: drive to reveal.
sentences.zh: 倾诉驱动力。

sentences.en: And it's fascinating because there's even some of these things are even illegal.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了，因为其中有些事情甚至还是非法的。

sentences.en: Now, the way we ask matters, right?
sentences.zh: 话说回来，我们提问的方式很重要，对吧？

sentences.en: So if we had asked face to face in an interrogation room, I don't know that people would be forthcoming.
sentences.zh: 如果我们是在审讯室里面对面地提问，我不知道大家还会不会这么坦诚。

sentences.en: But the way we asked these, we asked it on a pseudo-anonymous online survey.
sentences.zh: 但我们提问的方式不同，我们是通过伪匿名的在线问卷来调查的。

sentences.en: So it was done in the comfort of your home.
sentences.zh: 所以这项调查是在你舒适的家中完成的。

sentences.en: You don't have someone staring there watching you, judging you.
sentences.zh: 没有人在那儿盯着你、看着你、评判你。

sentences.en: In one set of studies, Leslie has examined whether people think less of those who have revealed
sentences.zh: 在一组研究中，莱斯利探讨了人们是否会看低那些吐露了

sentences.en: unsavory things about themselves.
sentences.zh: 自身不光彩事情的人。

sentences.en: Obviously, the answer is yes, right?
sentences.zh: 显而易见，答案是肯定的，对吧？

sentences.en: Not necessarily, which is pretty shocking.
sentences.zh: 不一定，这其实挺让人震惊的。

sentences.en: So what we did in this study was we asked people, let's say, we asked, who would you rather
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这次研究中做的是，我们问大家，比方说，我们问：

sentences.en: hire?
sentences.zh: 你更愿意雇佣谁？

sentences.en: And candidate A, one of the questions they had been asked on this intake survey was, have
sentences.zh: 对于候选人A，这份入职问卷中曾问过他这样一个问题：

sentences.en: you ever been reprimanded at work?
sentences.zh: 你曾在工作中受过训斥吗？

sentences.en: Yes, no, choose not to answer.
sentences.zh: 是，否，选择不回答。

sentences.en: We, of course, constructed these profiles ourselves.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些个人简介都是我们自己捏造的。

sentences.en: So candidate A, to the question, have you ever been reprimanded at work, says yes, just goes
sentences.zh: 所以候选人A对“你曾在工作中受过训斥吗”这个问题回答了“是”，直接

sentences.en: out and says the worst thing.
sentences.zh: 把最糟糕的事情说了出来。

sentences.en: Candidate B, on the other hand, clicked the choose not to answer box.
sentences.zh: 而候选人B则勾选了“选择不回答”。

sentences.en: So here we have a choice.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有了一个选择。

sentences.en: The participants had a choice.
sentences.zh: 参与者们有一个选择。

sentences.en: Would you prefer someone who admits something bad, that they've been reprimanded at work,
sentences.zh: 你更倾向于录用一个承认了糟糕事情（比如在工作中受过训斥）的人，

sentences.en: to someone who simply but very conspicuously refrains from answering, says, I'm not telling
sentences.zh: 还是一个只是非常明显地拒绝回答、说“我才不告诉你

sentences.en: you, I'm opting out, I'm concealing, essentially.
sentences.zh: 、我选择退出、我本质上在隐瞒”的人？

sentences.en: And it turns out that again and again, people prefer the revealer.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，一次又一次，人们更喜欢那个坦白的人。

sentences.en: They prefer the person who admits to the thing, even if it's a bad thing, relative to someone
sentences.zh: 他们更喜欢那个承认事情的人，哪怕这是一件坏事，而不是那种

sentences.en: who opts out of answering, who very saliently says, I'm not doing this.
sentences.zh: 选择不回答、极其显眼地表示“我才不干这事”的人。

sentences.en: In fact, you find something along the same lines when it comes to romantic relationships
sentences.zh: 事实上，当涉及到恋爱关系时，

sentences.en: as well.
sentences.zh: 你也会发现类似的情况。

sentences.en: Yes, that, so we did this the first time we got these results.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是这样——当我们第一次得到这些结果时，

sentences.en: We thought, this, is this a false positive?
sentences.zh: 我们心想：这是真的吗？这会不会是个假阳性结果？

sentences.en: This is nutty noodle, as my late grandmother would say.
sentences.zh: 正如我已故的祖母常说的那样，这简直荒谬透顶。

sentences.en: But so we did it again with other questions, other samples, other scenarios.
sentences.zh: 但我们又用其他问题、其他样本、其他情境重新做了一遍。

sentences.en: And one of the ones we tried was in the realm of dating, where what we did was we asked people,
sentences.zh: 我们尝试的其中一个领域是在约会交友方面，我们的做法是询问人们：

sentences.en: which of these two people would you prefer to date, person A or person B?
sentences.zh: 这两个人里你更愿意和谁约会，A先生还是B先生？

sentences.en: And one of the questions was, have you ever filed a false insurance claim?
sentences.zh: 其中一个问题是：你曾提交过虚假的保险索赔吗？

sentences.en: And person A ostensibly has said, frequently.
sentences.zh: A先生表面上回答说：经常。

sentences.en: So they're saying the worst possible thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说的是最糟糕的可能情况。

sentences.en: The other person, person B, has clicked choose not to answer.
sentences.zh: 另一个人，也就是B先生，点击了“选择不回答”。

sentences.en: And again and again, people, they'd rather date someone.
sentences.zh: 一次又一次，人们宁愿和这样的人约会。

sentences.en: Now, neither of these is fine specimens.
sentences.zh: 当然，这俩都不是什么完美的人选。

sentences.en: My father used to always say that.
sentences.zh: 我父亲以前总是这么说。

sentences.en: That's a fine specimen.
sentences.zh: 那可真是个“奇葩”标本。

sentences.en: Yeah, neither of them are someone you want to take home to your parents.
sentences.zh: 对，他们俩都不是那种你想带回家见父母的人。

sentences.en: But if push came to shove, right, if you're in this tight bind, which would you choose?
sentences.zh: 但如果事出紧急、逼不得已，对吧？如果你陷入这种两难境地，你会选哪个？

sentences.en: Because that's deeply revealing of human nature behind it.
sentences.zh: 因为这深刻地揭示了背后的某种人性。

sentences.en: And again and again, we prefer the revealer.
sentences.zh: 一次又一次，我们更偏爱那个坦白的人。

sentences.en: And what do you think this is telling us?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这说明了什么？

sentences.en: Why is it that we are so averse to the hider, even when the only option is a revealer who tells us that they've done something wrong?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们如此反感隐瞒者，哪怕唯一的选择是一个坦白自己做过错事的人？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great question.
sentences.zh: 对，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And we did many, many studies to try to understand why this was happening and why it was not happening.
sentences.zh: 我们做了许许多多的研究，试图弄清楚为什么会发生这种情况，以及为什么没有发生另一种情况。

sentences.en: In the end, what we discovered was that the preference for a revealer is driven by a global character judgment.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们发现，人们对坦白者的偏爱是由对个人整体品格的判断驱动的。

sentences.en: The person who conceals is not to be trusted.
sentences.zh: 选择隐瞒的人是不值得信任的。

sentences.en: So much so that we'd rather date someone, we'd rather employ someone, we'd rather even sit next to the subway besides someone who comes clean,
sentences.zh: 以至于我们宁愿和这样的人约会、宁愿雇佣这样的人、甚至宁愿坐在地铁里挨着一个肯坦白的人，

sentences.en: even if it's not the greatest thing to say.
sentences.zh: 哪怕他说出的并不是什么最光彩的事。

sentences.en: So researchers have found that several cognitive biases shape our desire to conceal.
sentences.zh: 因此研究人员发现，几种认知偏差塑造了我们隐瞒的欲望。

sentences.en: One of them is called the impact bias.
sentences.zh: 其中之一被称为“影响偏差”。

sentences.en: What is the impact bias, Leslie?
sentences.zh: 什么是影响偏差，莱斯利？

sentences.en: Yeah, so the impact bias is how we tend to overestimate the longevity of emotional events.
sentences.zh: 对，影响偏差是指我们往往会高估情感事件的持续时间。

sentences.en: So we think that when we break up with someone or if someone breaks up with us, we think we're going to be down in the dumps for a very, very long time slash eternity.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为，当我们和某人分手，或者有人和我们分手时，我们会陷入情绪低谷非常非常长的时间，甚至直到永远。

sentences.en: When reality, when that happens, like we're often surprised to see like, yeah, it sucks, but we're better sooner than we think.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，当那种情况发生时，我们往往会惊讶地发现：是的，这确实很糟，但我们恢复得比想象中要快。

sentences.en: Similarly, we think the highs last longer than they do.
sentences.zh: 同理，我们也会认为快乐的高峰期比实际持续得更久。

sentences.en: Like, you know, we get a raise.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，我们加薪了。

sentences.en: We think we'll be like feeling amazing for a really long time, but that we quickly adapt and it quickly subsides.
sentences.zh: 我们以为这种美妙的感觉会持续好久好久，但我们很快就会适应，这种感觉也很快就会消退。

sentences.en: So the impact bias refers to how we overestimate the duration and intensity of emotional events.
sentences.zh: 所以影响偏差指的是我们如何高估了情感事件的持续时间和强度。

sentences.en: The impact bias ends up shaping what we regret and also the difference between short-term regrets and long-term regrets.
sentences.zh: 影响偏差最终决定了我们后悔什么，以及短期遗憾和长期遗憾之间的区别。

sentences.en: In one study, the psychologists Thomas Gilovich and Victoria Medvek explored this difference.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，心理学家托马斯·吉洛维奇（Thomas Gilovich）和维多利亚·麦德韦克（Victoria Medvec）探讨了这种区别。

sentences.en: It's really fascinating because what they found was that in the short run, we tend to regret the things we did that resulted in bad outcomes, so-called sins of commission.
sentences.zh: 这真的很奇妙，因为他们发现，在短期内，我们往往会为自己做了导致糟糕结果的事情而感到后悔，也就是所谓的“作恶之憾”。

sentences.en: So in disclosure language, it's you say something, maybe you're a little tipsy, you say something, you feel like you go a little bit too far at a dinner party.
sentences.zh: 用坦白的专业术语来说，就是你说了些话，也许你当时有点微醺，说了一些话，让你觉得自己在晚宴上有点过头了。

sentences.en: The next morning, you have a massive disclosure hangover where you're that gut-wrenching, oh, why did I do that?
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，你就会经历巨大的“坦白后遗症”，那种揪心的“我当初为什么要说那些”的感觉，

sentences.en: And you just want to hide, and that sucks.
sentences.zh: 让你只想躲起来，那感觉糟透了。

sentences.en: And so we regret that a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对此悔恨不已。

sentences.en: So in the short run, right after, we regret the things we do, the regrettable things that we did.
sentences.zh: 因此在短期内，也就是事情发生后不久，我们最后悔的是我们做过的事，那些令人后悔的举动。

sentences.en: But in the long run, the pattern flips such that what we end up regretting much more over the course of our lives,
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，这种模式会发生逆转，在漫长的人生岁月中，我们最终更后悔的

sentences.en: the things that we didn't do, the sins of omission, the things that we didn't do that we should have done,
sentences.zh: 反而是那些我们没有做过的事，也就是“不作为之憾”，那些我们本来应该做却没有做的事情，

sentences.en: those are the things that leave us thinking, what if, what if I had told my college crush that I was into him?
sentences.zh: 这些才是让我们陷入沉思的事：如果……如果我当时告诉大学里暗恋的人我对他的感觉会怎样？

sentences.en: Like, what if, why didn't I do that?
sentences.zh: 就像，如果……我当时为什么不那么做呢？

sentences.en: What would be the harm?
sentences.zh: 这么做会有什么坏处吗？

sentences.en: And what are the missed opportunities?
sentences.zh: 错失的机会到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: Meanwhile, we don't ruminate at all over the long haul about, okay, maybe I, maybe I was rebuffed by this person,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，从长远来看，我们根本不会去纠结：好吧，也许我，也许我被这个人拒绝了，

sentences.en: but at least I found out, you know, you get kind of closure and you don't continue perseverating.
sentences.zh: 但至少我弄清了真相，你知道的，你会有一种尘埃落定的感觉，不会再没完没了地纠缠下去。

sentences.en: There was a book by the hospice care nurse, Bronnie Ware, titled The Top Five Regrets of the Dying.
sentences.zh: 临终关怀护士布朗妮·韦尔（Bronnie Ware）曾写过一本书，名为《临终前最后悔的五件事》。

sentences.en: What were these regrets, Leslie?
sentences.zh: 莱斯利，这五件事都是什么？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Bronnie Ware, my hero, she has spent, as a palliative care nurse,
sentences.zh: 布朗妮·韦尔，我的偶像，作为一名姑息治疗护士，她花了很多

sentences.en: she spent time, a lot of time with people at the very end of their lives.
sentences.zh: 很多时间陪伴那些生命垂危的人。

sentences.en: So she gets to know them a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以她对他们非常了解。

sentences.en: And she wrote a book where she collated her observations on what people tended to regret.
sentences.zh: 她写了一本书，整理了她对人们往往会后悔的事情的观察。

sentences.en: So on their dying beds, what did they say they regret?
sentences.zh: 那么在临终病榻上，他们说自己最后悔的是什么呢？

sentences.en: And here are the top five regrets.
sentences.zh: 以下就是最后悔的五件事。

sentences.en: I wish I'd had the courage to live a life true to myself, not the life others expected of me.
sentences.zh: 第一件：我希望当初我有勇气过真正属于自己的人生，而不是别人期望我过的人生。

sentences.en: Number two, I wish I hadn't worked so hard.
sentences.zh: 第二件：我希望自己当初没有那么拼命工作。

sentences.en: Number three, I wish I'd had the courage to express my feelings.
sentences.zh: 第三件：我希望自己当初有勇气表达真实的感受。

sentences.en: Ding, ding, ding, ding, ding.
sentences.zh: 完全说中了。

sentences.en: Number four, I wish I had stayed in touch with my friends.
sentences.zh: 第四件：我希望自己曾经和朋友们保持联系。

sentences.en: Number five, I wish I had let myself be happier.
sentences.zh: 第五件：我希望自己当初能让自己过得更快乐一些。

sentences.en: And so you can see four out of five of them are regret over things we didn't do that we wish we had done.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到，其中五分之四都是对我们没做却希望自己做了的事情的遗憾。

sentences.en: And one of them especially is that is one related to not sharing more of ourselves, not expressing our feelings.
sentences.zh: 其中有一件尤为突出，那就是关于没有更多地展现自我、没有表达自己真实感受的遗憾。

sentences.en: You say that you yourself were inspired to engage in more self-disclosure by Bronnie Ware's book.
sentences.zh: 你说过，你自己受了布朗妮·韦尔那本书的启发，从而开始进行更多的自我坦白。

sentences.en: Tell me about a recent incident with your mother where in some ways you were made aware, if you will, of all the things that you hadn't told her.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲最近发生在你母亲身上的一件事吧，在某种程度上，这件事让你意识到了所有你一直没有对她说过的事。

sentences.en: Oh, geez.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah, this was this was a scary episode.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一段极其吓人的插曲。

sentences.en: It was it was Christmas Day and my husband and I had just finished spending a lot of the day cooking in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 那是圣诞节当天，我和丈夫刚在厨房里忙活了大半天做饭。

sentences.en: Thanks to grandparents who took care of our little boys.
sentences.zh: 多亏了祖父母帮忙照顾我们的小男孩们。

sentences.en: And we are putting the turkey on the table and my mom looks gaunt.
sentences.zh: 正当我们把火鸡端上桌时，我妈妈看起来面容憔悴。

sentences.en: She says, I'm really not feeling well.
sentences.zh: 她说：“我真的觉得很不舒服。”

sentences.en: Something's just come over me.
sentences.zh: “我突然有种奇怪的感觉。”

sentences.en: I got to go lie down.
sentences.zh: “我得去躺一会儿。”

sentences.en: So she went to go lie down.
sentences.zh: 于是她去躺下了。

sentences.en: We serve the stuff and then I go upstairs to find her and I find her in the bathroom, clearly having vomited and looking at me with this glazed look of like unclear who I was.
sentences.zh: 我们把东西端上桌，然后我上楼去找她，结果发现她在浴室里，很明显刚吐过，她呆滞地看着我，眼神迷茫得似乎认不出我是谁了。

sentences.en: And so I grabbed her and I held her in my arms like a baby.
sentences.zh: 于是我一把抱住她，像抱婴儿一样把她揽在怀里。

sentences.en: And as soon as I did that, her eyes rolled back in her head and she went limp.
sentences.zh: 我刚一这么做，她的双眼就往上一翻，整个人瘫软了下来。

sentences.en: And I thought that she had died in my arMs.
sentences.zh: 当时我以为她死在我的怀里了。

sentences.en: And.
sentences.zh: 然后。

sentences.en: I just I sprang up and I bolted out the door.
sentences.zh: 我一下子跳起来，夺门而出。

sentences.en: I said, call 911.
sentences.zh: 我喊道：“快叫911！”

sentences.en: My husband's calling 911.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫正在拨打911。

sentences.en: I bolt out the door to our neighbor, who's a nurse.
sentences.zh: 我冲出门去找我们的邻居，她是一名护士。

sentences.en: And I bang, bang.
sentences.zh: 我拼命敲门，拼命地

sentences.en: I'm banging on their windows and she comes and she right away she runs in.
sentences.zh: 敲打他们的窗户，她听到了马上就跑了过来。

sentences.en: And then we get to the bathroom where my mom was and my mom looks at us like, what's all the fuss about?
sentences.zh: 然后我们赶到我妈妈所在的浴室，我妈妈看着我们，一副“你们在大惊小怪什么”的表情。

sentences.en: What are you doing?
sentences.zh: “你们在干嘛？”

sentences.en: I'm fine.
sentences.zh: “我很好。”

sentences.en: She was fine.
sentences.zh: 她确实没事。

sentences.en: It turned out that she we think it was food poisoning.
sentences.zh: 结果证明——我们觉得那是食物中毒。

sentences.en: And apparently when you vomit so violently, it can disrupt what's called your vagus nerve, which like overstimulates it.
sentences.zh: 显然，当你吐得那么厉害时，会扰乱所谓的迷走神经，也就是过度刺激了它。

sentences.en: And the way you need to kind of reset your brain by passing out.
sentences.zh: 而你需要通过昏厥来让大脑重置。

sentences.en: That's my layperson version of it.
sentences.zh: 这是我这个外行人的理解版本。

sentences.en: But oh, my gosh, that was so terrifying.
sentences.zh: 但天哪，那实在是太吓人了。

sentences.en: But it really it really reminds me like my mother at the time was 74.
sentences.zh: 不过这真的提醒了我——我母亲当时74岁。

sentences.en: Super spry.
sentences.zh: 超级敏捷。

sentences.en: She's still super spry.
sentences.zh: 她现在依然超级敏捷。

sentences.en: It really reminded me that I know it's cliche to say, but it's so true that you never know when your time is coming.
sentences.zh: 这真的提醒了我，我知道说这话是个陈词滥调，但却是如此真实：你永远不知道死神何时会降临。

sentences.en: And so with disclosure, what that means is that, like, don't hold back.
sentences.zh: 所以对于坦白来说，这意味着：不要有所保留。

sentences.en: Like, don't hold back telling someone all the ways you love them.
sentences.zh: 比如，不要吝啬向某人表达你爱他们的所有方式。

sentences.en: And so I ended up writing this, like, love list, this list of things to my mom about all the ways I love her.
sentences.zh: 所以我最终写了这个，算是爱的清单吧，这是一份写给我妈妈的清单，列举了我爱她的所有方式。

sentences.en: And all the big things and all the little things.
sentences.zh: 有所有的大事，也有所有的小事。

sentences.en: And yeah, it was really important to me.
sentences.zh: 是的，这对我真的很重要。

sentences.en: Did you read the letter to her or did you give her the letter?
sentences.zh: 你是把这封信读给她听的，还是直接把信交给了她？

sentences.en: I put it in her stocking.
sentences.zh: 我把它塞进了她的长筒袜里。

sentences.en: And it had all kinds of things in it, like big things.
sentences.zh: 里面有各种各样的事情，比如一些大事。

sentences.en: For example, I'm so grateful and I love the way she and my father, they always say, I mean, we are very lucky in that we had, you know, we weren't wealthy,
sentences.zh: 例如，我非常感激，我也很喜欢她和我父亲总是说——我的意思是，我们在某种程度上非常幸运，你知道的，我们虽然不算大富大贵，

sentences.en: but we definitely were comfortable.
sentences.zh: 但也绝对衣食无忧。

sentences.en: And so we were in a privileged position to be able to pursue our interests.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们处于一种优越的地位，能够去追求自己的兴趣。

sentences.en: And my parents really, really encouraged that.
sentences.zh: 我的父母真的、真的很鼓励这一点。

sentences.en: They said, always pursue what you're interested in.
sentences.zh: 他们说，永远去追求你感兴趣的事物。

sentences.en: And I feel that I got to this amazing place called Harvard doing what I love doing because fundamentally, you know, I worked hard, but I pursued my interests.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我能进入哈佛这个了不起的地方，做着我喜欢做的事，因为归根结底，你知道的，我付出了努力，但我也是在追随自己的兴趣。

sentences.en: And I got a lot of luck and all those other things.
sentences.zh: 而且我运气很好，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But the kind of life, the important life lessons I'm so grateful for.
sentences.zh: 但那种生活，那些我心怀感激的重要生活经验。

sentences.en: And then the small stuff too, like, oh, I love how she, this, oh my gosh, she, so I love gummy candies and what my, but I'm very particular on the colors.
sentences.zh: 还有一些琐碎的小事，比如，噢，我喜欢她这样，哦天哪，她，我喜欢软糖，而且我的要求，我对颜色非常挑剔。

sentences.en: I like the green ones, if they're lime, not apple.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢绿色的，如果是青柠味的，而不是苹果味的。

sentences.en: And I love the red ones.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢红色的。

sentences.en: And so when she comes to visit us, she gives me a bag of jujubes, gummy bears with curated just the colors I like.
sentences.zh: 所以当她来看望我们时，她会给我带一袋枣椰丸软糖或小熊软糖，这些都是精心挑选过的我喜欢的颜色。

sentences.en: She picks out the ones I don't and eats the dregs and then she gives her daughter like, oh, yeah, it's amazing.
sentences.zh: 她把我不喜欢的挑出来，自己吃掉剩下的残渣，然后把它送给她的女儿，噢，太棒了。
